sentences.text:
This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER 1. This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, for grant of anticipatory bail.

The applicant is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.546/2022 registered at Police Station Gandhinagar, District Indore for an offence punishable under Sections 420, 409 & 120-B of the IPC.

2. As per the prosecution, Premshree Prime Properties Private Limited for the purpose of development of its project Corridor Exotica received money from the complainant Shivendra Singh and similar prospective purchasers for the purpose of constructing and selling flats to them in the Anil Bhatewara vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132824438/
1 project.

sentences.text: Total amount received by them was Rs.5,47,98,146/-.
However the flats were not constructed, completed and handed over to the complainants on time nor were the sale deeds with respect to the same executed in their favour.
They were thus deprived of physical possession of the flats.

Premshree Prime Properties Private Limited had mortgaged the land of the project with M.P.
Finance Corporation which has to recover a sum of Rs.1,098.94 Lakhs from it.
The Directors of the company are Prashant Jain and Rajkumar Jain out of which Prashant Jain has expired in the year 2017 after which Nirbhay Singh has been inducted as a Director.
The company instead of investing the funds in the constructions of the flats has misappropriated a huge part of the same.

It has transferred substantial amount of funds to Arihant Devcon (India) Private Limited which is having three Directors and the present applicant is also an authorized signatory of the bank account of the said Company.

Substantial funds have been transferred to the account of Arihant Devcon (India)
Private Limited from the account of Premshree Prime Properties Private Limited and certain amount has been repaid also.
The allegation against the applicant is hence that he also benefited from misappropriation of funds from the account of Premshree Prime Properties Private Limited Company.

entities.text: Premshree Prime Properties Private Limited Company
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
He is neither the Director nor a person actively involved in the functioning of the Company.
In form No.32 which is being submitted by Arihant Devcon (India) Private Limited only two Directors have been mentioned who are Prashant Jain and Rajkumar Jain.
He has only been shown as a Non-Executive Director of the Company.
He does not have any role to play in the day to day affairs of the Company and no amount has been withdrawn from the account of the said Company for the personal use of the applicant.
The applicant is not employed in any capacity in that Company.
There is no direct evidence of involvement of applicant and there is no allegation against him that he has forged any documents.
The applicant has not received any amount from either of the two Companies in his individual bank accounts or by way of cash.

During investigation, the applicant was issued notices under Section 41-A of the Cr.P.C. by the Investigating Officer and he has appeared before him as and when directed and has extended full co-operation and shall continue to do the same and shall also co-operate in the trial.
It is hence submitted that the applicant be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.

4. The aforesaid prayer has been opposed by the learned counsel for the respondent/State as well as learned counsel for the objector by submitting that the applicant was as much involved in the entire matter of misappropriation of the account from the company as other accused hence he is also equally liable as the other co-accused.

He was involved in the day to day activities of Arihant Devcon (India) Private Limited Company and has transferred amount from the same to his private bank account and also by way of cash which he has put to his personal use.

The bank accounts have to be recovered from which only the siphoning of amount to the applicant would be ascertained hence there is requirement of custodial interrogation of the applicant who does not deserve to be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the case dairy.

sentences.text: 6. The applicant is stated to be a Director of Arihant Devcon (India) Private Limited Company.
However, from the documents on record, it appears that he was shown to be a Non-Executive Director and the Directors of the said Company are Prashant Jain and Rajkumar Jain.
It does not appear that the applicant is involved in the day to day functioning of the said Company or that he is a full time Director of the same.
The applicant is not a Director of Premshree Prime Properties Private Limited but a Non-Executive Director of Arihant Devcon which is a different legal entity.
The applicant also does not appear to have transferred the funds to his individual account or by way of cash.

From the record, it is seen that notice under Section 41-A of the Cr.P.C. has been issued to the applicant and he has appeared before the Investigating Officer and co-operated in the investigation and has assured to co-operate in future also.
Thus in my opinion, the applicant deserves to be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.

7. It is directed that in the event of arrest of applicant by the Arresting Officer, he shall be released on bail subject to his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac only)
with one surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
This order shall be subject to the condition that the applicant shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 30.01.2023 and shall continue to so appear before him as and when directed to do so.
Any failure on his part to comply with this condition shall entail in this order automatically coming to an end.
8. The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.
Applicant shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
9. Accordingly, Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.2142 of 2023 stands allowed and disposed off.
Certified copy as per rules.
